Safe as houses

By: Johann Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Many of us use private security companies to guard our loved ones and our assets. But how do we know if they can deliver on their promises?

Summary:
The SAPS is understaffed and underpaid. To report a break-in at your house is an exercise to get a number for the insurance claim, the police simply cannot affor the time or manpower to investigate anything less than very serious crimes. And so we've seen the blossoming of the private security industry to a level where they are even hired by the state to safeguard the police stations. But how safe are we when we use these services. These guards have acces to your property, are not questioned by anyone if they are on your property, know what alarm system you use and when you are not there.More and more cases are coming to the fore where these guards were involved in the break-ins. We investigate

Further information:
We have footage of members of a well-known security company's guards assisting in a house break and in a shop robbery. We also have case numbers of numerous other robberies where members of the same security company were involved in committing crimes. We also plan to expose the level of threat by asking known corrupt security guards to assist in a planned robbery.

By constitution it is the duty of the state to provide safety and security to the citisens of the the country. But they have failed in doing so, to a level where everyone who can afford it has had to install their own security systems and hire their own private security firms to do the work of the police. But how do we make sure that the company we hire to guard us is using clean guards? The short answer is that we don't know. Most companies have a very strict selection process when they hire security staff, checking a national data base for previous offences, checking qualifications and documents of the applicant and even doing polygraph tests. But none of these are foolproof, and sometimes even if a guard is caught in the act, he is simply fired by company A and then ends up working for company B in the same neighbourhood a month or two later. many of these guards are not even South African citisens, making it even more difficult to know if they really are who they say they are. Government is in the process of changing legislation about ownership of companies in this sector, and while many see it as a step in the right direction, critics are fearing that this will lead to even more problems - problems whic wil directly affect your and my safety.

Case Study:
Nic Matzopoulos

Expert:
Mr. Jason Holdstock

Locations:
Gauteng

Other Footage Sources:
Security cam footage of Chubb guards assisting with break-ins

Hidden Camera: Yes
Reason for hidden camera: We know who some of these corrupt guards are, and we intend approaching them to ask for assistance with a robbery we're planning in their neighbourhood.

Legal: Yes
Reason for legal: To ensure that we deal correctly with possible right of reply and entrapment issues.

Press Release:


Safe as houses
Could the armed response guards who have access to your home be criminals in uniforms? Exclusive footage leaked to Carte Blanche exposes the brazen way in which guards from a prominent security company rob unsuspecting clients.


Script:


Opening sequence


The most recent crime statistics reflect an interesting trend in robberies over the past four years. So called common robberies have gone down by just over a thousand reported cases while robberies with aggravating circumstances have increased by almost 18 000 cases.
It’s no surprise then that private security companies have become an integral part of our everyday lives, and even the police use armed response companies to guard police stations against criminals.
It’s a massive industry and driving down the streets of suburbia you are greeted by wall upon wall, supporting kilometre upon kilometre of electrical fencing and razor wire.
Link 1 Devi
So you now have a contract with one of the big players. You've installed beams, infra-red eyes, security cameras and an alarm loud enough to wake the dead. The security company guarantees an armed response in less than three minutes. So, you must be safe, right? Not neccessarily...
Little falls sequence
It was the Saturday morning just before Christmas. Andre Post was sitting on his veranda assembling his daughter’s Christmas gift. His neighbour Nic, was away for the weekend when Andre noticed Nic's gardener loading goods onto the back of a bakkie, with the help of another neighbour's gardener.
Andre
He actually said “Hi, how are you? I'm heading off home” And I thought why is he talking to me? We've never ever spoken to each other before.

Later, Nic's security cameras would show that the gardener, who had been working for Nic for 15 years, was busy robbing him.
Nic
He was part of the family. I mean, some nights he would sit here with us. When we go out to restaurants we'll take him with us. Part of the family. When we go to the dam, normally he goes with. So I mean, I feel really betrayed.

Although Nic uses another company for his security, the footage clearly showed that a Chubb security vehicle was involved in the proceedings.
Nick
We saw a Chubb vehicle in the morning. Came to our premises. He drove past our premises, by the main gate. We saw him there. He stopped. He looks in the yard, and he left. Couple of minutes later you can see him clearly come past my house, with a red bakkie following him. He makes a turn and the red bakkie stops in front. So then you actually see the red bakkie revers into where the gate is, and Chubb is standing on the side. And that is when now when the other three guys were in here and they were already putting all the stuff on the side. That is when they start loading now. And you can see, like I said, item for item, that is going outside our yard. They're actually now putting onto the vehicle.
Andre
Before I thought further I saw Nic's own security company, proceeding up the road, and I thought now let's see what happens here. Without hesitation the Chubb gentleman strolled over to him, and they had a chat, and then Nick's security company proceeded to leave. And I thought to myself, oh everything is kosher, there is not a problem here.
Nick
At the one stage, Chubb's vehicle was in my neighbour's property. And that is when the neighbour came, and Chubb was there. Chubb had to reverse, and came forward, and while he was talking to my neighbour, they were loading his car with tv's, camping equipment and all this
Devi: In the vehicle?
In the vehicle. Camping chairs. I bought new camping chairs, all my stuff is brand new. Heaps of clothes, because the laundry is downstairs. So you can see how they are taking heaps and heaps of my clothing, putting it in the vehicle.
Andre
And this vehicle departed, and it wasn't gone long, I thought, maybe ten minutes. Ten minutes and the vehicle was back.
Nick
We had over R300 000 worth of stuff in the garage. And the sad thing is, we actually started renovating the house, so a lot of the things – and I did room by room, so, I actually, we bought new appliances and things like that. New tv, new sound system, new washing machine. So I put everything down in the garage, because we were busy painting.

The suspects were arrested and are still in custody. But Nick is still waiting to see if his insurance company is going to pay out.
Link Devi
Of course, it's not only houses which get robbed

During our investigation into an Ethiopian hijacking syndicate in November last year, we showed how a warehouse was robbed of clothing worth millions over a weekend. It was evident that the security guard on duty had helped the thieves.
Jason
So as security industry we have to take risk steps. We have to put the guys on integrity tests, we have to do our own ITC checks, our own credit checks on the guys, our own criminal checks on the guys. To confirm that he actually is the person that we want to employ. He may have the papers to say so, but you find out that he's either bought the paperwork, or he swoped it out with his brother who looks identical, and then you need to be able to figure out with all your investigation, is this the right person, the right calibre, does he have the right qualifications, to actually perform the functions that you want him to perform.

Security guards are blacklisted if found guilty of any criminal act, but because this guard fled the scene and was not arrested, they couldn’t add his name to the list. And he may very well be working for the security company guarding your business tonight.

What we have as our security industry. We can only talk about our own experience, what we find is that a lot of security guys that come forward, have either been fired for theft from a different company, or had some sort of illegal activity prior.

The December holiday period is peak season for armed response assisted robberies. The owners are away and the guards are often the only people trusted to look after their homes.

This shop closed early on Christmas eve. But just minutes before midnight, the alarm was triggered when robbers entered the store.
It is interesting to note the ineffectiveness of the pepper spray the owner installed.
When they finally figured out where the alarm box was, they simply destroyed the wiring.
What the camera doesn't show, is how they used angle grinders to cut open and empty an ATM on the shop floor.
According to Chubb Security’s alarm activation report, the same guard went out three times to investigate what had repeatedly triggered the alarm. He could not access the back door, but according to his report, everything else seemed normal. We managed to track down a person with intimate knowledge of this specific robbery.
Swazi
The response team, that is supposed to be the one that is putting max security within the premises, is the one that is involved also with the criminals. And you may find out that some of the staff are also involved.

The problems normally start when a corrupt guard has to attend to an alarm activation at your property.
Swazi
Sometimes you find, that they press the panic button by mistake during the day.
So they have to go there, inside, and check what is going on.
Then they'll see that there is stuff there, or they see the money, lost of money coming in.. They'll take that information to the robbers that is doing the strategy on how they're going to hit that place

They would note where your sensors are placed, how your fences work, and with help from the control room, they could even print out your profile.
Swazi
They know that you're not around. Maybe you have travelled overseas for a certain period. They will have that information.

At this stage the only thing they probably don't know, is where the alarm box is.
Swazi
Because they are not the technicians that fit the alarm. So mostly, they don't know where the motherboard of the alarm is. But they know exactly the beams, the zones of the sensors.

On the day, they would use untraceable phones to call the robbers.
Swazi
If ever they go there, it happens that the alarm goes on, the signal will go to the control. The control will send the same Chubb guy.
The Chubb guy, before he even approaches the premises, he will have to call these criminals, so that he tells them to move out of the premises. So that when he comes there, he is find nobody inside.

It is important for the robbers to find and destroy the alarm system before they leave, as this would enable them to return after the guard has gone.
Swazi
He'll check as usual if there is nothing wrong. Then he reports that there is no break in that he could recognise within the premises.
Devi Link
Chubb's core business is to protect their clients, so when there are questions about their business, one would think that they do have an obligation to provide answers.

We asked Chubb for an interview, and even supplied them with the relevant case numbers and questions relating to these incidents.
They declined to appear on camera and ignored our questions on these two break-ins.
Instead, they sent us a document outlining their policy on appointing guards and how they treated incidents like these.
They also did not answer our question about how many similar incidents there have been in recent months involving Chubb guards. They added that it would be unfair for them to comment on footage they hadn’t seen.

Of course not all security guards are crooked, but a chain is only as strong as its weakest link. Even our insider on these robberies, says he would think twice before allowing armed response companies to guard his property.
Swazi
I will not allow these response teams to have full access to my premises. I really don't trust them.

And, understandably, Nic shares his sentiments.
Nic
I would think that just securing your property, to make sure that we are safe. I mean, build a pit around your house and put crocodiles in there, and don't have any security companies.










1. 10secs
You protect your property with 6-foot walls, electric fences & state of the art security... AND you pay for armed response on top of that. But are you safe?
 
2. 15secs
What do you do when the armed response guards protecting you, turn out to be criminals in uniform?
"Build a pit around your house and put crocodiles in there. And don't have any security companies. "
 
3. 15secs
Do you know as much about your security company as they know about you?
"They'll take that information to the robbers who are working out the strategy on how they are going to hit the place"
 Alternative:
Can you trust the security company looking after you, your loved ones and your home?
"They'll take that information to the robbers who are working out the strategy on how they are going to hit the place"

But none of these are foolproof, and sometimes even if a guard is caught in the act, he is simply fired by company A and then ends up working for company B in the same neighbourhood a month or two later. many of these guards are not even South African citisens, making it even more difficult to know if they really are who they say they are. Government is in the process of changing legislation about ownership of companies in this sector, and while many see it as a step in the right direction, critics are fearing that this will lead to even more problems - problems whic wil directly affect your and my safety.
